questions.stem: A Kafka consumer writes feature rows to Postgres. The team wants no lost and no duplicated rows after crashes. Which combination achieves that most simply?
options: Commit offsets before the write so a crash never reprocesses
Commit offsets after the DB transaction commits, and make the write an upsert on a natural key
Enable the idempotent producer on the gateways
questions.explanation: At-least-once delivery (commit after the durable write) plus an idempotent write keyed on a natural id gives effectively-once results. Committing first loses data on a crash; the idempotent producer only removes duplicates between producer and broker.

questions.stem: Which two statements about enable.idempotence=true on a Kafka producer are true? (choose two)
options: It prevents duplicate records in a partition caused by producer retries
It makes the consumer's database writes idempotent
It turns at-least-once consumers into exactly-once consumers
questions.explanation: The idempotent producer dedupes retries per partition and needs acks=all. It says nothing about what your consumer does with the data downstream.

questions.stem: Gateways key messages by device id. Why does that matter for the consumer?
options: It spreads one device across all partitions for throughput
All of a device's messages land on one partition, so per-device order is preserved
It lets the broker compact old messages
It is required for consumer groups to work
questions.explanation: The partitioner hashes the key; one key always maps to one partition, which is the only place Kafka guarantees order.

questions.stem: A backfill of 2026-10-14 is rerun after a partial failure and the day ends with 1.3x the expected rows. What is the root design flaw?
options: The write is a plain INSERT, not idempotent per natural key
The day was not partitioned by hour
questions.explanation: A backfill must be safe to rerun: upsert or replace-partition semantics keyed on (device, window). Retries then cannot double count.

questions.stem: A data quality check counts windows per device per day for completeness. The archive contains some duplicate lines. What must the check count?
questions.explanation: Duplicates would inflate completeness and hide a gap. Count distinct keys.

questions.stem: Gateway firmware 4.2 adds a field firmware to every message. The consumer's Pydantic model is strict and starts quarantining every message. Which is the best fix?
options: Configure the model to ignore unknown fields and version the schema (BACKWARD compatible changes)
Catch ValidationError and write the raw dict
questions.explanation: Adding an optional field is a backward-compatible change; consumers should tolerate unknown fields. A schema registry enforces the compatibility rule at publish time.

questions.stem: Which MQTT QoS level guarantees a message arrives at least once, possibly duplicated?
questions.explanation: QoS 1 is at-least-once; QoS 2 is exactly-once between client and broker (expensive); QoS 0 is fire-and-forget. Retained messages are about the last value per topic.

questions.stem: A Python ingest service spends most of its time waiting on the broker and an HTTP enrichment API. Which concurrency model fits best?
options: multiprocessing with one process per message
asyncio with bounded concurrency and timeouts on every call
A busy loop polling every millisecond
questions.explanation: I/O-bound work suits asyncio (or a small thread pool); every external call needs a timeout and concurrency needs a bound.

questions.stem: Which two belong in the CI gate of a production Python service repo? (choose two)
options: pytest with property-based tests for parsers
pip install --upgrade of every dependency on each run
Disabling tests that touch time zones
questions.explanation: Types, lint and tests (including Hypothesis for parsers and signal functions) belong in CI. Unpinned upgrades break reproducibility; a lock file (uv) is the fix.

questions.stem: A consumer rejects messages with naive timestamps (no UTC offset). A colleague asks why not just assume local time. The best answer:
options: The idempotency key is built from window_start; a guessed offset makes the same window two keys around DST changes and across sites
Naive timestamps are larger on the wire
questions.explanation: Keys must be stable. Guessing time zones creates duplicate or colliding windows (DST, multi-site).

questions.stem: An accelerometer samples at 2 kHz. A 1.3 kHz gear-mesh tone is present at the sensor and there is no anti-alias filter. Where does it appear in the spectrum?
questions.explanation: Nyquist is fs/2 = 1 kHz. A tone above it folds to |f - fs| = |1300 - 2000| = 700 Hz.

questions.stem: Where must anti-aliasing happen for a sensor stream that will be sampled or decimated?
options: Before sampling (analog) or before dropping samples (digital low-pass)
questions.explanation: Once a tone has folded it is indistinguishable from real content. Filter before sampling or before decimation.

questions.stem: You compute an FFT over 4096 samples at 20 kHz. What is the bin spacing?
questions.explanation: Frequency resolution = fs / N = 20000 / 4096 = 4.88 Hz.

questions.stem: Why apply a Hann window before the FFT of a vibration window?
options: It reduces spectral leakage from the discontinuity at the window edges
questions.explanation: Windowing tapers the edges so a tone that is not bin-centred does not smear across the spectrum; it slightly widens the main lobe.

learn.label: The Scientist and Engineer's Guide to DSP

questions.stem: Vibration teams summarise spectra with Welch's method rather than one long FFT. Why?
options: It is the only method SciPy supports
Averaging overlapping windowed segments lowers the variance of the PSD estimate
questions.explanation: Welch trades resolution for a much less noisy estimate by averaging periodograms of overlapping segments.

questions.stem: A bearing outer-race defect on a pump does not show a line at BPFO in the raw spectrum, only a hump near 3 kHz. What reveals BPFO?
options: The envelope spectrum: band-pass around the resonance, Hilbert envelope, then the spectrum of the envelope
questions.explanation: Each impact rings a structural resonance; the defect rate modulates that resonance. Demodulating (the envelope) turns sidebands into a line at BPFO and its harmonics.

questions.stem: Which two features rise sharply for impulsive signals such as early bearing damage? (choose two)
questions.explanation: Impulses make the tails heavy (kurtosis well above 3) and the peak large relative to RMS (crest factor).

questions.stem: scipy.signal.filtfilt works well offline but is wrong on the live gateway stream. Why?
options: It is zero-phase, so it needs future samples (non-causal) and pads each chunk edge
questions.explanation: Zero-phase filtering runs forwards and backwards over the whole signal. Streaming needs a causal filter with its state carried between chunks.

questions.stem: BPFO + BPFI equals which quantity for a rolling-element bearing?
options: Number of balls x shaft speed
questions.explanation: BPFO = n/2 fr (1 - r) and BPFI = n/2 fr (1 + r); their sum is n fr.

questions.stem: A firmware update multiplies every raw sample by 1.6. Which detector scores are unaffected?
options: An absolute RMS threshold in raw counts
A peak-to-median ratio in dB on the spectrum
Band energy in raw counts squared
questions.explanation: A uniform gain cancels in any ratio; absolute thresholds in raw units move.

learn.label: The Scientist and Engineer's Guide to DSP

questions.stem: Shaft speed on a variable-speed pump drifts from 25 to 32 Hz. What keeps BPFO-based detection valid?
options: A fixed BPFO band computed at 29.5 Hz
Recompute defect frequencies per window from a tachometer or a 1x speed estimate (order tracking)
questions.explanation: Defect frequencies scale with shaft speed; track speed or resample to orders.

questions.stem: A promotion gate compares challenger and champion. Which design avoids comparing apples to oranges?
options: Use each model's validation metric from its training run
Evaluate both on the same fixed holdout set (hash checked) in the same job
Use the metric with the most recent timestamp for the model name
questions.explanation: Same data, same code, same job. Metrics from different runs or datasets are not comparable.

questions.stem: The eval step crashed but CI continued (|| true) and the gate read the latest metrics for the model name, which belonged to the previous version. What two changes close the hole? (choose two)
options: Fail the eval step on error (non-zero exit)
Bind metrics to the exact model version and holdout hash, and fail closed when missing
Use >= instead of > in the comparison
questions.explanation: A gate that cannot find the challenger's own metrics must reject (fail closed). Silent eval failures must fail the pipeline.

learn.label: MLOps: continuous delivery and automation pipelines (Google Cloud)

questions.stem: Why use registry aliases (champion, challenger) rather than hard-coded version numbers in the serving config?
options: Promotion and rollback become moving a pointer, with history, without redeploying config
questions.explanation: Aliases decouple deployment from version numbers and make rollback a one-line change.

questions.stem: For a pump-fault detector, which pair of metrics should the gate use? (choose two)
questions.explanation: Faults are rare, so accuracy is meaningless (always 'healthy' scores 99%). The business cares about catching failures and not crying wolf.

questions.stem: Input drift is detected on three pumps after a seasonal temperature change. What should happen first?
options: Retrain automatically on the last week
Investigate: check whether prediction quality (confirmed outcomes, alert rate) changed and why
Roll back to the oldest model
questions.explanation: Drift is a signal to investigate, not an automatic retrain trigger; retraining on unlabelled shifted data can make things worse.

questions.stem: Which practice makes any registered model rebuildable months later?
options: Version the training data (DVC or table snapshots) and record its hash, code commit and params on the run
Tag the model with the author's name
questions.explanation: Lineage needs data, code and parameters. The artifact alone cannot be reproduced or audited.

questions.stem: According to 'Hidden technical debt in ML systems', most of a production ML system is:
options: Infrastructure around it: data collection, features, serving, monitoring, configuration
questions.explanation: The model is a small box in the middle; the surrounding pipeline is where debt and failures live.

learn.label: Hidden technical debt in ML systems

questions.stem: The first model ever for a site has no champion. What should the gate do?
options: Require it to clear absolute thresholds agreed with the client (recall, false alarms, latency)
questions.explanation: With no champion, compare against the agreed absolute bar (and the baseline process).

questions.stem: A challenger ties the champion on recall and false alarms. With a strict-improvement rule, what is the outcome and why can that be right?
options: Reject: promotion carries risk and cost, so it needs evidence of benefit
questions.explanation: Non-inferiority rules are possible but must be explicit. A tie with >= quietly promotes untested changes, as in the stale-metric incident.

questions.stem: Which serving option fits a plant with intermittent WAN and 10 gateways?
options: A cloud REST endpoint called per window
On-device inference with the model shipped as a versioned artifact
Batch scoring in the cloud once a week
questions.explanation: Local inference keeps working offline; the registry still governs which version each device runs.

learn.label: MLOps: continuous delivery and automation pipelines (Google Cloud)

questions.stem: After static INT8 quantization the model's recall collapses from 0.91 to 0.35, but FP32 is fine. Preprocessing at runtime applies a StandardScaler outside the graph. What is the most likely cause?
options: INT8 is not supported on ARM
The calibration data reader fed raw unscaled features, so activation ranges were calibrated on the wrong distribution
questions.explanation: Calibration must see exactly what the model sees at runtime. Wrong input scale means wrong scales and zero points everywhere.

questions.stem: What is the difference between dynamic and static quantization in ONNX Runtime?
options: Dynamic quantizes only weights ahead of time and activations at runtime; static needs calibration data to fix activation ranges ahead of time
questions.explanation: Static (QDQ) usually gives better latency on CPUs/NPUs but needs representative calibration data.

questions.stem: Which two belong in an honest edge benchmark? (choose two)
options: Warm-up runs, then p50 and p95 latency at batch size 1
Size, latency and accuracy reported together for FP32 and INT8
questions.explanation: Edge inference is usually batch 1; tail latency matters; a smaller faster model that is wrong is not a win.

questions.stem: A TensorRT engine built on a Jetson Orin is copied to a Jetson Xavier and fails to load. Why?
options: TensorRT engines are tied to the GPU architecture and TensorRT version they were built with
questions.explanation: Ship the ONNX model and build (or cache) engines per target; or use the ORT TensorRT EP with an engine cache.

questions.stem: One ONNX file must run on an Intel-based industrial PC and an NVIDIA Jetson. What does ONNX Runtime offer?
options: Execution providers (OpenVINO, CUDA/TensorRT, CPU) selected at session creation for the same model
questions.explanation: Execution providers let the same graph use vendor accelerators, with CPU fallback for unsupported ops.

questions.stem: After exporting an sklearn pipeline with skl2onnx, what is the first check before quantizing?
options: Parity: ONNX FP32 outputs match sklearn within a tolerance on real inputs
questions.explanation: Prove the export is correct before optimising it, otherwise quantization errors and export bugs mix.

questions.stem: A colleague sets intra_op_num_threads to 16 on a 4-core ARM gateway that also runs the feature pipeline. Likely effect?
options: Oversubscription: worse and noisier latency for both inference and the pipeline
questions.explanation: Match threads to available cores and the workload mix; measure.

questions.stem: Which graph optimization level should you use when you want to ship a pre-optimized model file to many identical devices?
options: Apply optimizations offline and save the optimized model, then load with minimal runtime optimization
questions.explanation: Offline optimization saves start-up time on devices; keep it per hardware target where EP-specific.

questions.stem: The client does multi-camera video analytics on NVIDIA Jetson. Which stack is most likely already in use?
questions.explanation: Vision on Jetson usually means JetPack, TensorRT and DeepStream pipelines.

questions.stem: INT8 model size dropped only from 13 KB to 10 KB. Why so little?
options: Small models are dominated by graph structure, metadata and Q/DQ nodes; weight savings show on larger layers
questions.explanation: Report the numbers honestly; on small models the latency and accuracy matter more than size.

questions.stem: A new model version is rolled out to 10 gateways. Which order is right?
options: All at once, roll back if anyone complains
Canary one device, gate on health and model metrics for N windows, then batches, automatic rollback on failure
questions.explanation: Same as a Kubernetes canary: limit blast radius, gate on real signals, roll back automatically.

questions.stem: During a rollout two devices are offline. How should the controller treat them?
options: Not as failures; they block phase completion until a timeout, then are reported and retried later
questions.explanation: Unreachable is not unhealthy. Rolling back the fleet because of a WAN blip is its own outage.

questions.stem: After a WAN outage, the cloud shows three times the alerts for line 2. The buffer generates event ids with uuid4 at send time. What is wrong?
options: The id is not stable across retries, so the server cannot dedupe resends after lost acks
questions.explanation: Assign the event id at capture (device + sequence or window) and dedupe on it server-side.

questions.stem: Why SQLite in WAL mode for the gateway's offline buffer?
options: It is the only embedded database
Readers and the writer do not block each other, and commits are durable and fast on small devices
questions.explanation: WAL lets the replay reader run while the capture path keeps writing; transactions make mark-as-sent atomic.

questions.stem: Which two help when gateways are on slow metered links? (choose two)
options: Send features and alerts, raw clips only on request
Cap the buffer on disk with an explicit drop policy that is reported
questions.explanation: Bandwidth and disk are budgets; make the trade-off explicit.

questions.stem: Why separate the model artifact from the application image?
options: Ship a new model (with version reported back) without rebuilding or redeploying the app, and roll back the model alone
questions.explanation: Model and code change at different rates; each needs its own version and rollback.

questions.stem: A site with no internet needs k3s on the gateways. What does the air-gap install use?
options: The k3s binary and the airgap images tarball copied to each node, plus a private registry if needed
Pulling from Docker Hub through USB tethering
questions.explanation: k3s documents an air-gap path with saved images; same idea for docker image save/load.

questions.stem: Device identity for 200 gateways should use:
options: One shared API key baked into the image
Per-device certificates issued at enrollment, revocable individually
No auth on the plant network
questions.explanation: Shared keys mean one leak compromises the fleet and cannot be revoked per device.

questions.stem: The rollout controller crashes halfway. What property lets it continue safely?
options: Its state (phase, touched devices, versions) is persisted and every step is idempotent, so it resumes
It waits for a human every time
questions.explanation: Controllers must be restartable; desired-state reconciliation (like ArgoCD) gives this naturally.

questions.stem: A/B partition (image-based) updates as in Mender give which main benefit on devices?
options: Atomic update with automatic fallback to the previous partition if the new one fails to boot
questions.explanation: A bad image cannot brick the device; the bootloader falls back.

questions.stem: pip on a client build box fails with 'certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate' through a TLS-inspecting proxy. The right fix:
options: Point pip (and every other client) at a CA bundle that contains the proxy's issuing chain plus the public roots
questions.explanation: The proxy re-signs traffic; clients must trust its chain. Disabling verification is a security finding, not a fix.

questions.stem: openssl s_client through the proxy shows a one-certificate chain issued by 'Corp Inspection Issuing CA 2' and verify code 20, with only the corporate root in the CAfile. What is missing?
options: The intermediate 'Corp Inspection Issuing CA 2' (the proxy does not send it)
questions.explanation: Code 20 means the chain cannot be built to a trusted root: an intermediate is missing.

questions.stem: Which NO_PROXY value correctly bypasses the proxy for every host under corp.internal?
questions.explanation: A leading dot (or the bare domain in most clients) matches subdomains; '*' disables the proxy for everything.

questions.stem: The site has no internet at all. Which two prepare a Python install? (choose two)
options: pip download (or a locked uv environment) into a wheelhouse for the target platform
Save container images to tar files with checksums
Ask the client to open the firewall for a day
questions.explanation: Build the field kit before you travel: wheelhouse, saved images, mirrored model files with checksums.

questions.stem: docker pull fails on a client host behind a proxy while curl works. Most likely:
options: The Docker daemon has its own proxy configuration; the shell's HTTPS_PROXY does not apply to it
questions.explanation: The daemon pulls images, not the CLI; configure the daemon proxy (and its CA) separately.

questions.stem: An edge assistant runs a small local model. Which tasks suit it best?
options: Long multi-step plans over many tools
Short tool-calling lookups and summaries grounded in tool results
questions.explanation: Small models do well on short, well-scoped tool tasks; route harder questions elsewhere when policy allows.

questions.stem: Which two belong in a hybrid edge-cloud router policy? (choose two)
options: Cloud only when a policy flag allows it
Never send raw site data to the cloud without approval
Always prefer the cloud for speed
Send everything to both and compare
questions.explanation: Residency and network policy are the client's; the router enforces them in code.

learn.label: Effective context engineering for AI agents

questions.stem: A plant manager asks for 'AI on the pumps'. What is the FDE's first deliverable?
options: A one-page brief: who has the problem, today's cost, the target metric and baseline, constraints, out of scope
questions.explanation: Frame the problem and agree the measurable outcome before code, so the result is not argued later.

learn.label: What are Forward Deployed Engineers? (The Pragmatic Engineer)

questions.stem: Which question follows The Mom Test when interviewing a maintenance planner?
options: Would you use an app that predicts failures?
Tell me about the last unplanned bearing failure: what happened and what did it cost?
How much would you pay for this?
questions.explanation: Ask about past behaviour and real costs, not hypothetical wishes.

questions.stem: Which handoff list makes the work customer-owned?
options: Code in their repo, model card, runbooks (retrain, roll back, add a device), an eval suite they can rerun, each with a client owner
questions.explanation: The client must be able to operate and change it without calling you.

learn.label: What are Forward Deployed Engineers? (The Pragmatic Engineer)

questions.stem: On site, a connection to the historian times out and the client's network team says 'the firewall is open'. Best next step?
options: Capture packets (tcpdump) on both ends to show where SYN/ACK stops, and share the evidence
questions.explanation: Evidence ends arguments; show exactly where the conversation stops.

questions.stem: An alert note typed by a contractor tells the assistant to raise a threshold, and the threshold changes. Where must the control live?
options: In the tool dispatcher: an explicit allow-list, write tools behind a human approval the model cannot satisfy
questions.explanation: Prompts are not enforcement. The model can call whatever the dispatcher will run.

questions.stem: The lethal trifecta has three legs. Which two of these options are legs? (choose two)
options: Access to private data and exposure to untrusted content
questions.explanation: Private data + untrusted content + a way to send data out. Remove one leg.

questions.stem: The assistant cites tool call 'c9' that never ran. What should the loop do?
options: Reject the answer as invalid and retry once with the error, then fail
questions.explanation: Citations are checked against executed calls in code; otherwise grounding is decoration.

questions.stem: Why return tool errors as data ({"error": ...}) instead of raising?
options: The model can read the error and correct its call (for example a valid machine id), and the loop stays in control
questions.explanation: Errors the model can act on, with the valid choices listed, are part of tool design.

questions.stem: Your eval suite for the assistant should start with:
options: Error analysis of real transcripts, then deterministic checks (schema, citations, tool calls) before any model-graded rubric
questions.explanation: Read outputs, categorise failures, then test the real failure modes deterministically first.

questions.stem: Which telemetry lets you debug a slow answer on the plant server?
options: A single log line per day
Spans per model call and per tool call with token counts and latency (OTel GenAI conventions)
questions.explanation: Trace each turn: model, tool, tokens, latency.

questions.stem: A small local model returns prose instead of the JSON object about 10% of the time. Best first fix?
options: Validate with Pydantic and retry once with the exact validation error; measure the rate in evals
questions.explanation: Validate-and-retry fixes most format errors; the eval tells you whether it is enough.

questions.stem: What does GGUF Q4 vs Q8 trade on an edge box?
options: Q4 halves memory and speeds up tokens per second at some quality cost versus Q8
questions.explanation: Quantization levels trade RAM and speed against quality; measure on your tasks and hardware.

questions.stem: A POST to create a work order times out. The server may have created it. How do you retry safely?
options: Retry with the same Idempotency-Key derived from the anomaly (machine + alert window)
Create a new key per attempt
questions.explanation: The server dedupes on the key, so a lost response cannot create a second work order.

learn.label: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs

questions.stem: Which errors should the client retry? (choose two)
questions.explanation: Retry transient errors with backoff and a budget; fix the request for 4xx; refresh the token on 401 once.

learn.label: Timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter

questions.stem: Why full jitter on exponential backoff?
options: It spreads retries from many clients so they do not hit the server in synchronized waves
questions.explanation: Synchronized retries cause thundering herds; jitter decorrelates them.

learn.label: Timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter

questions.stem: A Python HTTP client in the integration has no timeout set. What happens on a half-open connection?
options: The call can hang indefinitely and block the worker
questions.explanation: Every external call needs connect and read timeouts (httpx makes them explicit).

questions.stem: A streaming band-pass reset on every 1-second chunk produces a spike at each chunk start on a DC-coupled accelerometer. Why?
options: Each chunk starts from zero state, so the +1 g gravity offset looks like a step that rings the filter
questions.explanation: Carry the filter state (zi) between chunks and initialise it to the steady state.
